title: Derived common-quotient reduction as a normalized strict tower
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:R\to B$ a flat morphism of commutative ring sheaves, and $J_1\supseteq J_2\supseteq\cdots$ ideal sheaves of $R$. Assume the maps induced by $\varphi$ identify $S_n=R/J_n$ with $B/J_nB$, compatibly with quotient transitions. Use the module categories, restriction, derived categories and K-flat derived scalar extension of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every $M\in D(B)$ there are canonical $S_n$-linear isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R^L S_n\cong M\otimes_B^L S_n.$$
Choose a single K-flat $B$-representative $P$ with flat terms. These isomorphisms are induced by the ordinary comparisons $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_R S_n\cong P\otimes_B S_n$, both identified with $P/J_nP$, and are natural in $M$. After restriction of all levels to $R$, the comparisons form an isomorphism of strict tower complexes, commute with all quotient transitions, and carry the strict quotient cone $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ to the corresponding cone. Here tensor products and their pure sections are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], and K-flatness and flat terms are [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. A strict tower here means an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] in the category of cochain complexes of sheaves of $R$-modules; its cone is a morphism from the constant tower on $\operatorname{Res}P$.

source.place: Tag 099L (section-derived-completion-noetherian), finite coefficient comparison; general flat common-quotient argument extracted by NE, using sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change).

proof.text: Represent $M$ by a $B$-complex $G$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] over $B$ to choose one quasi-isomorphism $P\to G$, with $P$ K-flat and all its terms flat over $B$. Flatness of $B$ over $R$ is precisely the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat], so $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat over $R$ and has flat $R$-terms. Restriction does not change the underlying abelian sheaves [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; kernels and sheafified cokernels are therefore unchanged, so it preserves this quasi-isomorphism. This same $P$ works simultaneously at every level; no compatible choice of separate resolutions is required.

For a term $F=P^i$, put $Q_n=F/J_nF$, the sheaf quotient by the submodule sheaf locally generated by products $jp$. By the tensor and sheafification universal properties [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the formulas
$$a_n:F\otimes_R S_n\longrightarrow Q_n,\quad p\otimes\bar r\longmapsto[rp],\qquad b_n:Q_n\longrightarrow F\otimes_R S_n,\quad[p]\longmapsto p\otimes1$$
define inverse $S_n$-linear maps. Indeed changing $r$ by $j\in J_n$ changes $rp$ by an element of $J_nF$, while $jp\otimes1=p\otimes\bar j=0$ makes $b_n$ well-defined. The composites fix $[p]$ and $p\otimes\bar r$, respectively, by tensor balancing. These formulas are first defined on presheaf sections and then sheafified; a section of $S_n$ need only lift locally to $R$. Thus no surjectivity on sections, nor enough points of the site, is assumed. The quotient itself is the sheafified cokernel [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafification of the elementary tensor-quotient formulas

proof.text:
Apply the preceding calculation with $B$ and its ideal $J_nB$. Its submodule $(J_nB)F$ equals $J_nF$: locally a generator $(\varphi(j)b)p$ equals $\varphi(j)(bp)$, and the reverse inclusion uses $b=1$. The assumed ring isomorphism $R/J_n\cong B/J_nB$ therefore identifies the second tensor with the very same $S_n$-module $Q_n$. Let
$$c_n:F\otimes_R S_n\xrightarrow{a_n}Q_n\xrightarrow{(a_n^B)^{-1}}F\otimes_B S_n.$$
Then $c_n(p\otimes s)=p\otimes s$, and its inverse has the same formula, checked locally after lifting $s$ to $R$. This also verifies $S_n$-linearity for the stipulated common-quotient structure. Equalities of maps are checked on pure sections by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus].

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); elementary balancing and quotient calculation

proof.text: Apply $c_n$ in every degree of the fixed $P$. Tensoring with the degree-zero sheaf $S_n$ has differential $d_P\otimes1$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Both composites in the chain-map square send $p\otimes s$ to $d_P(p)\otimes s$; the same calculation for the inverse proves that $c_n$ is an isomorphism of complexes. More generally, for a $B$-linear chain map $h:P\to P'$ the two naturality composites send $p\otimes s$ to $h(p)\otimes s$. The pure-section determination property [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] makes these equalities actual equalities of sheaf morphisms.

For $J_{n+1}\subseteq J_n$, write $t_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$ for the quotient map. The quotient-transition square for $c_{n+1}$ and $c_n$ has both composites
$$p\otimes s\longmapsto p\otimes t_n(s).$$
The compatibility assumed for the common-quotient identifications ensures that the same $t_n$ is used over $R$ and over $B$. Restrict the targets to $R$. The adjacent squares, and hence their composites for all levels, give an isomorphism of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system], degreewise and compatible with the differentials by step 4. The quotient maps from $P$ are chain maps $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and satisfy $(1\otimes t_n)(p\otimes1)=p\otimes1$. Finally $c_n(p\otimes1)=p\otimes1$ proves equality of the two strict cones from the constant tower, at every level, rather than only after localization. Pure sections determine these squares [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus].

source.place: Tag 099L (section-derived-completion-noetherian), explicit finite-reduction transitions and units

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] for $R\to S_n$ and $B\to S_n$. Step 1 supplies its K-flat models on both sides, so the complexes of step 4 represent $\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R^L S_n$ and $M\otimes_B^L S_n$ as objects of $D(S_n)$. Their chain isomorphism thus gives the asserted canonical $S_n$-linear derived isomorphism. To check naturality and independence of the chosen resolution, regard both ordinary constructions as functors on $B$-complexes with values in $D(S_n)$. Their comparison is natural by step 4. On the class of K-flat $B$-complexes with flat terms both functors invert quasi-isomorphisms, by flat restriction and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1); every complex has a resolution in that class by step 1. The universal derived-functor construction [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] therefore descends this natural isomorphism uniquely, and its inverse descends as well. This gives naturality for all morphisms of $D(B)$ and the canonical agreement for a different $P$. Step 5 already proves the stronger strict representative assertion, including quotient transitions and cones.
